notes: All three personas found the decision lesson strong and the AI lesson weak. Selin cannot say what the AI did (product.selin.json, learnedAboutAI). The hackathon judge calls use of AI the weakest part and asks for proof that a real owner tried it. The educator wants a predict-then-check moment and a closed loop. The pattern: What-IF stops at the test card. Two things stay invisible: what comes after (reality against the guesses) and who did what (owner, code, AI). And no real café has used it yet. The Berlin closed beta can fix all three. Prove the loop with 10 cafés. Keep the AI's role explicit now that /try lets owners skip the AI. Recruit around one real, dated Berlin decision.
improvements: 1. What: Make the Berlin beta prove the whole loop, not just the report. Each of the first 10 cafés runs one real 10-day test from its card and comes back on day 10 to see where reality landed next to its three guesses. That comparison becomes What-IF's central lesson: 'your guess was a guess, your count is a fact, and no AI could have known it'. Why: vision.md 'How to measure progress' names exactly these signals: the owner explains the assumptions, finds the test feasible, tries it and returns to compare. Vision core step 6 is also the clearest edge over 'ChatGPT with a template'. The hackathon judge found the loop never shown and the question 'would you believe a real owner tried it?' unanswered. The educator asked for predict-then-check and a closed loop in the demo. Selin's 'maybe' rests on the card being runnable on paper. Smallest version: add a 'log your result' screen at the end of /try in de/en/es/pl. It takes the baseline, average lunch customers, deals sold and 'usually has lunch here' strokes, writes them into the same /r#token, and the existing resultBlock (src/report/sections.ts:401) draws 'Where reality landed'. The test card also offers an .ics download with the day 3, 5 and 10 check-ins (nothing stored). Before the first invite, write down what the beta must show: how many of 10 owners say their break-even in their own words, start the test and come back with counts. Risk: owners do not come back after 10 days, and the stateless design means the founders never see a result. Ask each owner whether she will send her result link to the beta contact; never collect it silently. Report counts ('4 of 10 cafés'), never percentages, and never turn results into a benchmark across cafés (vision: no invented local statistics).

2. What: Make 'who did what' a constant, visible part of every report, so the AI lesson survives /try. Show three lines from the owner's own report: from you, 13 numbers; calculated by plain code, the figures; guesses, 4, which only your test can check; done by an AI, asked the questions and played the customers, or nothing at all on /try. Then give one rule to take home: 'Next time any AI gives you a number, ask where it came from: is it yours, calculated, a guess or imagined?' ('Woher kommt diese Zahl?'). Why: the hackathon judge's verdict, 'weakest: use of AI'. All three personas caught the contradiction 'played by an AI' against 'with no AI' (report.txt:516, 524), and Selin's learnedAboutAI ends with 'I am not sure what the AI actually did'. The educator lists 'an AI played these customers, or no AI did' as a misconception the report risks. The beta makes this urgent: /try reaches a report with no AI at all, so without the ledger the product drifts into a calculator and loses the theme. Smallest version: build a 'Who did what' card at the top of step 1 from the share state (source: /try or coach; rehearsal method: rule-based, in-context or subagents), and take the rehearsal caveat from the same field. Add one AI lesson to 'What you learned', and a glossary entry in all four languages: 'KI-Modell / AI model: explains and plays roles; it does not know your future'. End /try with an honest offer that says what an AI coach would add: the questions and imagined customers played by an AI, never a better forecast. Risk: it becomes a lecture Selin skips between customers, so keep it to three lines with counts from her own report. It could also make AI-played customers sound more credible than rule-based ones; keep the Imagined chip and 'not data' on both.

3. What: Recruit and serve the first 10 cafés around one real, dated Berlin decision every owner faces now. The minimum wage rises from €13.90 to €14.60 on 1 Jan 2027, so the beta opens with 'Was wäre, wenn ich meine Preise anpasse?' (the price-change template), next to the lunch deal. Anything What-IF cannot model yet, such as hiring or Sunday hours, gets an honest 'not yet, here is the method on paper' instead of the nearest template. Why: this is what makes it more than ChatGPT with a template. The owner's own Z-report numbers meet dated public facts with sources, and code does the maths and ends in a test with a stop rule. That serves vision core step 3 ('Add relevant context') and 'Evidence beside advice', which the shipped demo lacks. Selin knows her numbers from the Z-report and needs a route she can finish alone. The hackathon judge asks for one real, dated session ('never invent a quote'). The mcp and skill judges found 'hire a part-timer' and 'what if it rains' sent to the lunch deal, although the README promises honesty about scope. Smallest version: write a German invite card with the question, the /try link and a per-café code. Build a Berlin price-change demo (flat white +€0.20) with the minimum-wage fact card (source and date). Add one engine figure beside the price-change result: what the wage rise costs a week, your hours paid at the minimum wage × €0.70, tagged as a guess until checked against payroll. Make pickTemplate answer 'not yet' for hiring and opening hours. Serve each café with one 30-minute session in German on the owner's phone, using her own Z-report, and keep a dated note of what she understood, written with her consent. Risk: it can read like tax or pay advice. Keep 'ask your Steuerberater', the 'not a substitute for an accountant' line, and the wage as a dated fact, never a recommendation to raise prices. Founder-led sessions inflate understanding: note whether a helper was present, and let at least three cafés use /try alone, then compare.
